epithet: Allah has heard the woman who pleads
lede: A wife came to the Prophet ﷺ with a grievance no court of her people would have listened to. ʿĀʾishah, in the same room, could not catch all she said. This surah begins: Allah has heard. It is the only surah in which His name is in every ayah.

names.name: al-Mujādilah
names.note: After Khawlah bint Thaʿlabah, who argued her case with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It is read both al-Mujādilah, the pleading woman, and al-Mujādalah, the pleading. It is also called Qad samiʿa, after its opening words.

revelation.detail: It is Madinan in the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, ʿIkrimah and the majority. Two partial exceptions are reported: from ʿAṭāʾ, that only its first ten ayat are Madinan; and from al-Kalbī, that all is Madinan except one ayah (58:7). Every subject it treats — a ruling on marriage, the conduct of gatherings round the Prophet ﷺ, the hypocrites and their allies — belongs to the community of Madinah.
revelation.when: Madinah, in the middle years, as the life of the new community was being ordered

evidence.quote: وَهِيَ مَدَنِيَّةٌ في قَوْلِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، والحَسَنِ، ومُجاهِدٍ، وعِكْرِمَةَ، والجُمْهُورِ. ورُوِيَ عَنْ عَطاءٍ أنَّهُ قالَ: العَشْرُ الأُوَلُ مِنها مَدَنِيٌّ، والباقِي مَكِّيٌّ
عَنْ عَائِشَةَ قَالَتْ: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي وَسع سَمْعُهُ الْأَصْوَاتَ، لَقَدْ جَاءَتِ المجادلةُ

setting: Among the Arabs before Islam a man could say to his wife, “You are to me as the back of my mother.” It was called ẓihār. It did not free her to marry anyone else; it simply made her untouchable to him, for as long as he liked. It was a way of discarding a woman while keeping her.

Aws ibn al-Ṣāmit, an old man and quick to anger, said it to his wife Khawlah bint Thaʿlabah. She went to the Prophet ﷺ. He had received nothing from Allah on the matter and could give her no release. She would not accept that; she had children — if I leave them with him they will be lost, and if I keep them they will go hungry — and she turned from him and said: O Allah, I complain to You.

ʿĀʾishah was there. “Praise be to Allah,” she said afterwards, “whose hearing takes in all voices. The woman who pleaded came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and spoke to him while I was at the side of the room, and I could not hear what she was saying. And Allah sent down: ‘Allah has heard the words of her who pleads with you about her husband.’” The practice was abolished, with a heavy expiation on any man who used it.

The rest of the surah deals with other things that were corroding the young community from inside: whispered consultations meant to unsettle the believers, a mocking greeting used by some of the Jews of Madinah, crowding at the Prophet’s ﷺ gatherings, and hypocrites who had taken as friends a people under Allah’s anger. It ends by defining the believers as “the party of Allah” — and loyalty to Him as something that outranks father, son, brother and clan.

occasions.title: Khawlah bint Thaʿlabah
occasions.text: “Blessed is He whose hearing encompasses everything. I could hear the words of Khawlah bint Thaʿlabah, though some of it was hidden from me, as she complained of her husband to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: ‘Messenger of Allah, he has consumed my youth and I have borne him children, and now that I am old and can bear no more, he has pronounced ẓihār on me. O Allah, I complain to You.’ She did not leave before Jibrīl had come down with these ayat.”
occasions.source: ʿĀʾishah: al-Nasāʾī (3460) and Ibn Mājah (2063); ṣaḥīḥ according to al-Albānī. Al-Bukhārī cites it without a chain in his Ṣaḥīḥ.

evidence.quote: عَنْ عائِشَةَ أنَّها قالَتْ: تَبارَكَ الَّذِي وسِعَ سَمْعُهُ الأصْواتَ، لَقَدْ جاءَتِ المُجادِلَةُ فَكَلَّمَتْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ، وأنا في جانِبِ البَيْتِ أسْمَعُ كَلامَها، ويَخْفى عَلَيَّ بَعْضُهُ

occasions.title: The twisted greeting
occasions.text: Some of the Jews came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, “al-sāmu ʿalaykum” — death be upon you — in place of the greeting of peace. ʿĀʾishah answered them sharply, and he said: “Gently, ʿĀʾishah; Allah loves gentleness in every matter.” The ayah speaks of those who “greet you with what Allah does not greet you with.”

aim: To make manifest Allah’s all-embracing knowledge and complete encompassing — to train people to be watchful of Him, and to warn against opposing Him.
themes: Loyalty and the party of Allah

outline.title: The plea, and the ruling
outline.summary: Allah has heard the words of her who pleads with you about her husband and complains to Allah; Allah hears the two of you conversing. Those who pronounce ẓihār: their wives are not their mothers. Whoever does so and then goes back on it must free a slave before they touch; or, if he cannot, fast two months in succession; or, if he cannot, feed sixty poor people.

outline.title: Those who oppose
outline.summary: Those who set themselves against Allah and His Messenger will be brought low, as those before them were. On the Day Allah raises them all, He will tell them what they did: He counted it, and they forgot it.

outline.title: Secret counsels
outline.summary: There is no private talk of three but He is the fourth of them, nor of five but He is the sixth, nor fewer nor more but He is with them wherever they are. Have you not seen those who were forbidden secret counsels and return to them, and greet you with a greeting Allah does not greet you with? Believers, when you confer in private, let it be for goodness and piety. Secret counsel of the other kind is from Satan, to grieve the believers — and he cannot harm them at all, except by Allah’s leave.

outline.title: In the gathering
outline.summary: When you are told to make room in the assemblies, make room; when you are told to rise, rise. Allah will raise those of you who believe, and those given knowledge, by degrees. And the charity that was asked before private audience with the Messenger was, in mercy, lifted from them.

outline.title: The party of Satan
outline.summary: Have you seen those who take as allies a people with whom Allah is angry? They are neither of you nor of them, and they swear to a lie knowingly, using their oaths as a shield. Their wealth and their children will avail them nothing. Satan has mastered them and made them forget the remembrance of Allah. They are the party of Satan — and the party of Satan are the losers.

outline.title: The party of Allah
outline.summary: Allah has written: “I will surely prevail, I and My messengers.” You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers or their kin. He has inscribed faith in their hearts and strengthened them with a spirit from Himself. Allah is pleased with them, and they with Him. They are the party of Allah — and the party of Allah are the successful.

keyAyah.why: The opening that names the surah. A complaint made in a low voice, by someone with no standing, was answered from above the seven heavens.

virtues.text: ʿĀʾishah said: “Praise be to Allah, whose hearing takes in all voices. Khawlah came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ complaining of her husband, and her words were hidden from me. Then Allah sent down: ‘Allah has heard the words of her who pleads with you about her husband.’”

before: Al-Ḥadīd ended with Allah’s bounty being in His hand alone. Al-Mujādilah begins with that bounty reaching a woman whom no one else could help.
after: Al-Mujādilah spoke of hypocrites who allied themselves with a people under Allah’s anger. Al-Ḥashr tells what became of that alliance when the Banū al-Naḍīr were besieged.

notable.label: No private talk of three but He is the fourth
Allah raises those who believe and those given knowledge

sources: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim; the Sunan of al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Mājah
